note: Authoritative machine-readable trust-crossing and control-ownership record for Decision #121. docs/architecture/distributed-execution-threat-model.md is a rendered view of these IDs. Every Critical/High crossing carries a release test (a REL-* owner ticket or a releaseTest field). ownerTickets reference defined backlog tickets in docs/replatform/program-design.md. Clause fields (authentication/authorization/confidentiality/integrity/revocation/audit) state what a crossing's control REQUIRES; they are a charter, not a report. `deliveryStatus` is the separate field that says whether the control has actually been built and measured -- delivered | not-delivered | unaudited -- and `deliveryEvidence` carries the backing. Before this field the two were indistinguishable, and a Critical crossing measured absent read exactly like one that holds. `unaudited` is the honest default for a crossing nobody has audited; it must never be upgraded to `delivered` except from a recorded measurement.

crossings.deliveryEvidence: not-delivered: MEASURED ABSENT at every candidate enforcement layer. Finding E8-F003 (open, HIGH, in scripts/finding-ownership.json) records the measurement: against REAL E2B sandboxes in workflow run 33857218680, with a positive control (the allowlisted host was reached) and an apparatus control (an RFC-2606 .invalid host failed), both of which held -- a host NOT on the declared egressAllowlist was reached from inside the sandbox that declared it, identically to a control sandbox that declared none; and 169.254.169.254 answered HTTP 401 from inside the guest, a live IMDSv2 token challenge rather than a dropped packet. E8-F003 further records that no enforcement exists at the provider level, the in-sandbox level (BRW-004 slice (f), not attempted), or the proxy level (classifyEgressDestination's only non-test consumer is a module nothing in production imports). This entry does not close DE-08 and does not close E8-F003; it only stops the register from asserting the opposite of what was measured.
